question: Which rectangle holds more area if both perimeters equal 100?
assumptions: Flat rectangles with side lengths in common length units
Both shapes drawn at the same physical pixel-per-unit scale

storyboard.motion: Two neutral outlines of 10×40 and 25×25 side by side on IDENTICAL pixel-per-unit scale, no area labels; tiny labels 10×40 and25×25.
Trace the outer edges with one traveling highlight; widths and heights clearly annotated.
Fill each shape with identical-size unit cells, right shape visibly 56.25% more area than left. Contrast color does not change size meaning.

storyboard.secondary_text: Stretch one side. Shrink the other.
storyboard.motion: Morph a rectangle continuously from w10,h40 to w25,h25 with P=100 maintained every frame; area grows via A=w(50-w), numeric label follows exact geometry.
Pause at square w25,h25; render clean A=625 and P=100. Close with visual, not a long equation.

caption:
Two rectangles can have exactly the same perimeter but different areas.

10 × 40 → perimeter 100, area 400
25 × 25 → perimeter 100, area 625

For rectangles with perimeter 100, width + height = 50, so area is w(50 − w). That is greatest when width and height are both 25.

The square has 225 more square units of area in this comparison. The drawing uses the same scale for both shapes.
